thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Unravels on Fears of US/China Trade War; Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory

title: Close Update: Wall Street Unravels on Fears of US/China Trade War; Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Unravels on Fears of US/China Trade War; Nasdaq Enters Correction Territory April 02, 2018, 04:42:59 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
Fears of an escalating trade war between the world's two largest economies sent Wall Street into a tailspin, driving the Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 below critical technical support and wiped out all of the Nasdaq Composite's gains for 2018. Although the major indices were off their worst levels by the close, the Dow was lower by more than 400 points, and the Nasdaq shed nearly 3%. 
In retaliation for US tariffs on imported steel and aluminium from China, Beijing announced tariffs on 128 products imported from the US totalling $3 billion. The major market averages all sold-off at the NYSE open, driving the volatility index to a 5-day high and placing the S&P 500 below its 200-day moving average by mid-morning and the Dow as much as 750 in the red. 
The Nasdaq was undermined by more threatening tweets against Amazon ( AMZN ) from President Donald Trump, a Tesla ( TSLA ) recall and April Fool's joke that backfired, Apple's ( AAPL ) alleged decision to ditch Intel ( INTC ) chips from its Macs, and a privacy issue that continue to plague Facebook ( FB ). The index fell to its lowest level in more than seven weeks and entered correction territory with a loss of almost 200 points. 
Economic data failed to generate interest in US equities as both the purchasing manager's and Institute for Supply Management's manufacturing indices were below expectations. Also, construction spending was up a paltry 0.1% in February, missing expectations for a 0.5% gain. 
Weighed down by broad-based losses across Wall Street, the energy sector was also down by close to 3% despite indications that US production has levelled off and on sanctions against Iran. 
The rotation into safe-havens lifted the price of gold by close to $20 and pushed Treasury yields lower across most of the curve with the exception of 3-month bills and the 30-year bond. The 10-year Treasury note richened to 2.71% before backing up before the close to 2.74%. 
Here's where the markets stood at the close:

S&P 500 was down 58.99 points (-2.23%) 
Nasdaq Composite Index was down 193.33 points (-2.74%)
